title: Linux Fundamentals & Command-Line Streaming Pipelines
summary: Master Linux POSIX filesystem navigation, file permissions (octal and symbolic), ownership, stream redirections, and multi-stage text processing pipelines with grep, sed, awk, cut, and sort.
learningObjectives: Navigate Linux directory hierarchies and audit file permissions using octal and symbolic modes.
Construct high-throughput POSIX streaming pipelines using grep, sed, awk, tr, cut, sort, and uniq.
Direct standard streams using POSIX redirections (stdout, stderr, append, pipes) to capture diagnostics.

curriculumModules.title: Linux Filesystem Hierarchy & POSIX File Security
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: POSIX permissions govern read, write, and execute permissions across user, group, and others. Critical system and Kubernetes configuration files must be locked down to prevent privilege escalation.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Enforce the principle of least privilege on node filesystems: restrict sensitive configuration files like /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf to 0600 root-only ownership and verify umask defaults.

curriculumModules.title: POSIX Streaming Pipelines & Text Manipulation Engines
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: UNIX stream architecture connects stdout to stdin across distinct utilities via pipes (|), allowing rapid log parsing and pattern filtering without writing intermediate disk files.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Construct robust triage one-liners using grep -E for error filtering, awk for field extraction, and sort | uniq -c for frequency distribution analysis in live incident response.

labs.title: Linux Filesystem Permissions & Security Hardening
labs.scenario: A security compliance audit flagged inappropriate permissions and ownership on critical Kubernetes configuration files. You must harden permissions and enforce strict access controls on /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf and /home/learner/.kube/config.
labs.productionContext: Exposing admin kubeconfig credentials with world-readable permissions allows unprivileged host processes to compromise the entire Kubernetes cluster.
objectives: Inspect file permissions on /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf using ls -la
Harden /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf to mode 0600 owned by root:root

steps.title: Inspect File Permissions
steps.instruction: Run `ls -la /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf` to check current mode and ownership.

steps.title: Harden Cluster Admin Kubeconfig
steps.instruction: Set permissions on `/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf` to `0600` and ensure ownership is `root:root`.

validationRules.description: Executed chmod command to harden kubeconfig permissions
Executed chown command to ensure root ownership

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure you run `chmod 600` on both kubeconfigs and `chown root:root` on `/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf`.

labs.title: POSIX Streaming Pipelines & Access Log Analysis
labs.scenario: Production ingress access logs in /var/log/nginx/access.log show intermittent 5xx spikes. You must construct a POSIX pipeline using grep, awk, sort, and uniq to isolate HTTP 500 error counts, and write the offending client IP summary to /home/learner/offenders.txt.
labs.productionContext: Streaming POSIX text processing pipelines allow SREs to triage multi-gigabyte log anomalies instantaneously without external tooling dependencies.
objectives: Inspect the raw access log structure using head -n 5 /var/log/nginx/access.log
Extract 500 errors, aggregate unique offending IPs, and redirect output to /home/learner/offenders.txt

steps.title: Aggregate HTTP 500 Offenders
steps.instruction: Filter lines with HTTP 500 status, extract client IP, count unique occurrences, and write to `/home/learner/offenders.txt`.

validationRules.description: Constructed grep and awk pipeline for log filtering
Offending client IP report written to /home/learner/offenders.txt
validationRules.remediation: Ensure output is redirected to `/home/learner/offenders.txt` using `>`.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Verify that `/home/learner/offenders.txt` contains the client IP `192.168.1.105` generated by the stream pipeline.

assessmentQuestions.question: What numeric octal mode represents -rw-r----- (read/write for owner, read-only for group, no permissions for others)?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Owner read (4) + write (2) = 6. Group read (4) = 4. Others none (0) = 0. Thus 640.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which POSIX operator redirects both standard output (stdout) and standard error (stderr) to a target file?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: &> or > file 2>&1 merges file descriptor 2 (stderr) into descriptor 1 (stdout) and redirects both streams into the destination file.
